Colombian Firm Unveils Modular Bridge Solution for Remote Infrastructure Projects

Bogotá, June 17—A Colombian engineering firm has launched a new modular bridge kit aimed at accelerating infrastructure development in remote and rural areas, the company said Monday, as the government seeks to expand connectivity across the country’s diverse terrain.

Constructora Andina presented the “PuenteXpress” system at an industry event in Bogotá, describing it as a lightweight, prefabricated steel bridge solution that can be transported by truck and assembled on-site within days. The product is designed to address the logistical challenges faced by builders in hard-to-reach regions, where conventional bridge construction can be hampered by rugged geography and limited access to equipment.

“The idea is to provide a reliable, cost-effective way to link communities and support local economies, especially in areas that have historically been isolated,” said Laura Medina, general manager of Constructora Andina. “Our modular system requires minimal heavy machinery and can be erected by a small team, making it ideal for Colombia’s rural departments.”

According to the company, each PuenteXpress bridge can span up to 40 meters and support vehicles weighing up to 30 tons, enabling the passage of trucks, ambulances, and agricultural machinery. The modular sections are fabricated at Constructora Andina’s facility outside Bogotá, then shipped to project sites throughout the country.

Industry analysts say the launch comes at a time of heightened government investment in rural infrastructure. President Gustavo Petro’s administration has pledged to improve road and transport links as part of its peace and development strategy, particularly in regions affected by conflict and underinvestment.

“This type of product could be a game-changer for Colombia,” said Camilo Herrera, an infrastructure consultant based in Medellín. “The ability to deploy bridges rapidly will help local authorities respond to seasonal floods and reconnect communities after landslides, which are common in the Andes and Pacific regions.”

The Colombian Chamber of Infrastructure welcomed the launch. “Innovative solutions like PuenteXpress are essential for closing the transport gap between urban and rural Colombia,” said María Fernanda Ruiz, the chamber’s spokesperson. She noted that over 12,000 rural communities lack all-weather road access, according to recent government data.

Constructora Andina said it has already received orders from three regional governments and expects the first installations to be completed in the coming months. The company plans to offer training programs for local construction teams to support the rollout.

“We believe this technology will improve lives and help drive economic growth outside major cities,” Medina said.
